events.text: Circa 1480 DR, the noted Turmishan sage Imani sponsored several groups of heroes to recover the staff, but although successful, it was stolen from him by an orc gang known as the Fangfists, this led to a four-way chase involving the Cult of the Dragon; a band of Zhentarim mercenaries; an agent of the Shadovar; and Imani's hired adventurers.

The Second Sundering, also known as the Sundering of Toril and Abeir, was a great catastrophic event in the history of the worlds of Abeir and Toril, that took place during the decade of the 1480s DR.
In 1483 DR, the city and its bridges were in disrepair.
The Battle for Eveningstar was a pivotal battle of the Sschindylryn invasion of Eveningstar that determined the course of the war from that point on.

The Battle of the Cold Vale was a battle of the War of the Silver Marches fought between the orcs of Many-Arrows and the Silver Marches, represented by the dwarves of Citadel Adbar, in the Year of the Awakened Sleepers, 1484 DR.
Cormyr entered a war with Sembia in defence of the Dalelands. It became a war on two fronts as Netheril invaded Cormyr's borders.
Land is exchanged frequently throughout the war as they battle across the three countries of Cormyr, Sembia and the Dalelands.
In the Year of the Awakened Sleepers, 1484 DR, the Darkening was cast over the region in preparation for the drow and orc invasion.
In the Year of the Awakened Sleepers, 1484 DR, the city's First Speaker was Jolen Firth.
By 1484 DR, however, the mythal was dying and Magadon Kest made contact with the mythal at the request of Drasek Riven.
In the Year of the Awakened Sleepers, 1484 DR, cracks began to appear in the shroud of darkness that covered Sembia.

The Shadovar invasion of Wheloon was a brief conflict fought inside the Wheloon Prison in the mid-1480s DR, which involved the forces of Thultanthar infiltrating the prison and attacking the defending Cormyrean garrison.

The Sschindylryn invasion of Eveningstar was a part of the War of Everlasting Darkness, which saw the Spider Queen Lolth send the drow city of Sschindylryn to war with Cormyr under the cover of the Darkening, primarily fought in the King's Forest and the village of Eveningstar.
In the Year of the Awakened Sleepers, 1484 DR, during the War of the Silver Marches, Sundabar was conquered by an orc army commanded by the warlord Hartusk and renamed Hartusk Keep.
The War of the Silver Marches was a conflict between the orcs of Many-Arrows and the cities of Luruar that took place in the Silver Marches over 1484 DR to 1485 DR.
The Great Rain was a weather event that struck central Faerûn as part of the Second Sundering.

By autumn of the Year of the Iron Dwarf's Vengeance, 1485 DR, the Kingdom of Many-Arrows had been erased, although the Many-Arrows tribe persisted as the most powerful orc tribe in the Spine of the World.
cites: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden, с. 111

events.text: By the Year of the Iron Dwarf's Vengeance, 1485 DR, the city had fallen to ruin, with monsters from the Evermoors thwarting efforts to rebuild it.
In the following year the Bedine of Anauroch revolted against their Netherese oppressors and regions of central and northern Faerûn became outright battlefields.
The Ritual of the March was an ancient ritual used by the dwarves of Delzoun to traverse great distances as a unified army.

The Battle of the Under Way, also known as Comragh na Uamh in Dwarvish, was a battle that took place in the Under Way of Gauntlgrym between the dwarves of Mithral Hall and the forces of the drow House Xorlarrin in the Year of the Nether Mountain Scrolls, 1486 DR, during the reclamation of Gauntlgrym.
The First Tymanther–Unther War was a conflict between the nations of Tymanther and Unther that took place in the Year of the Rune Lords Triumphant, 1487 DR.
King Foril died in his sleep.

Crown Prince Irvel Obarskyr went missing due to a teleportation mishap, dying days later from his injuries. Irvel was secretly resurrected by Havilar, moving him by law to the end of the line of succession.
Raedra served as regent whilst Baerovus Obarskyr was comatose after the Netherese attack. Upon recovery he was promptly crowned, but soon abdicated when his father returned.

On 14 Uktar, during the Siege of Suzail by Netherese forces King Irvel Obarskyr sacrificed himself in a charge against a wyvern, disguised through illusions as Thauglorimorgorus the Purple Dragon. His daughter Raedra killed the 'Purple Dragon Reborn'.
On the Feast of the Moon, the Siege of Suzail was broken when the army of the Western Marches arrived from Arabel to slaughter the remaining Shadovar army.
On 5 Nightal, it was decided that Raedra Obarskyr would be crowned queen, due to her brother's abdication. Baerovus was willingly made an advisor.

The only other living Obarskyr, Erzoured, enjoyed his new-found popularity with the army as a war hero and did not attempt to claim the crown. His past schemes and well-known desire for the throne were not forgotten by the new Queen.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 11

events.text: Cormyr survived the war and successfully reclaimed its land, unlike the destroyed Netheril. Queen Raedra focused on rebuilding the country, instead of expansion.

Around the Year of the Nether Mountain Scrolls, 1486 DR, Neverember's efforts to rebuild the city began to bear fruit, although reconstruction would continue for at least another decade. He ordered the use of magical means to seal the Chasm, although at a huge expense to the city's coffers that other parts of the city were neglected for years.
Circa 1486 DR, the archmage Gromph Baenre of Menzoberranzan, tricked by Lolth, used a powerful summoning ritual that allowed many demon lords from the Abyss to walk the Underdark of Faerûn.
The Mulhorandi rebellion was a revolt against the rulers of High Imaskar, led by the wizard Nezram the World-Walker and the gods of the Mulhorandi pantheon in the late years of the 15th century DR.
In 1487 DR, after years of war against Netheril, Thultanthar fell upon Myth Drannor, destroying both cities and thereby the second Cormanthyr.
In the Year of the Rune Lords Triumphant, 1487 DR, King Frostmantle's seventh wife, Concettina Delcasio, was abducted by Malcanthet, the Queen of the Succubi.

In the Year of the Rune Lords Triumphant, 1487 DR, after the most direct effects of the Spellplague had ended, Halruaa was returned to Toril as part of the Second Sundering, not via weaving another forceweb, nor via sacrifice, but through chaos that followed the Second Sundering.
In 1487 DR, after years of war against Netheril, Thultanthar fell upon Myth Drannor, destroying both cities.

After over 100 years of war against Netheril, the Netherese enclave of Thultanthar fell from the sky upon Myth Drannor, destroying both cities. Ilsevele and her surviving subjects fled to Semberholme.
In the Year of the Rune Lords Triumphant, 1487 DR, the young and aggressive vampire Kirenkirsalai restored the Night Masks underneath the city and became a force to be reckoned with.
In 1487 DR, Lantan was returned to Toril as part of the Second Sundering, and Lantanese ships began to travel again to the Sword Coast.
By 1489 DR, the human slaves of Calimshan had overthrown their genasi masters with the aid of a Chosen of Ilmater.
In 1489 DR, Dambrath was a nation of nomadic human clans, primarily horse riders.
Around 1489 DR, Kreeg was aging and another leadership transition was expected soon.
Around 1489 DR, Thavius Kreeg was aging and another leadership transition was expected soon.
The Everlasting Rime was a period of nonstop winter in Icewind Dale created by Auril, goddess of cold and ice, in the late 1480s DR.
By 1489 DR the dale was once again free and independent.
In 1489 DR, political tensions arose when Grauman, the ruling king at the time, made preparations to pass his the throne to his son Taumarik.
In response to increasing dragon and cultist activity, the Council of Waterdeep was formed around 1489 DR, bringing together representatives of realms from all across the Sword Coast.
By the Year of the Warrior Princess, 1489 DR, Impiltur had regained much of its former importance among the lands of the east, despite its many troubles.
By 1489 DR, though the landmass of Samarach had returned, the civilization was no longer believed to exist.
By 1489 DR, High Mage Taern Hornblade had stepped down as ruler of the city and Methrammar Aerasumé took over as Lord of Silverymoon.
By the Year of the Warrior Princess, 1489 DR, tensions between Vaasa and neighboring Damara were nearing a boiling point.
In 1491 DR, an elemental codex was stolen from Earthfast by Furgis Boltsmelter.
In mid-Mirtul of 1491 DR, numerous Masked Lords and other people were gruesomely assassinated as part of Braethan Cazondur's conspiracy to seize control of the city.
By 1491 DR, Neverember's efforts to rebuild the city proved successful, and Neverwinter had slowly been restored as a center of civilization in the Sword Coast North.
In the Year of the Scarlet Witch, 1491 DR, a Zhentarim-protected caravan en route to Triboar was attacked by members of the Cult of the Howling Hatred.

The Absolute crisis was a series of events that transpired throughout the Western Heartlands and Sword Coast in the late 15th century DR, when the cult of the Absolute rose to power and caused great chaos across the region.
In the Year of Three Ships Sailing, 1492 DR, Baldur's Gate was caught up in the plot of an illithid elder brain named the Absolute and its cult.

In the Year of Three Ships Sailing, 1492 DR, over a few months, Kreeg coaxed Grand Duke Ulder Ravengard of Baldur's Gate to come to Elturel to resolve several disputes that had troubled the two cities for some time.
The Gralhund Villa Bloodbath was the name given by Waterdhavian newspapers to an attack on Gralhund Villa by members of the Zhentarim in the Year of Three Ships Sailing, 1492 DR.

In the Year of Three Ships Sailing, 1492 DR, volence erupted in the streets and backrooms of the city as competing factions searched for former Open Lord Dagult Neverember's embezzled hoard of gold, guided by the Stone of Golorr.

In the Year of Three Ships Sailing, 1492 DR, a number of agents and organizations including the shady Xanathar's Thieves' Guild, the greedy Zhentarim, the enigmatic Harpers, and even the stalwart Lords' Alliance sought to recover a cache of 500,000 gold dragons that was hidden somewhere within the city, a sum that was embezzled by the ousted former Open Lord of the city, Dagult Neverember.
By the Year of the Duplicitous Courtier, 1496 DR, he had begun levying hefty taxes specifically against wealthy merchants and adventuring companies in order to fund further rebuilding efforts.
High King Derid Kendrick sought a formal peace treaty with Thuven Moltenbeard, the fire giant king of Oman's Isle. A fomorian known as Ulrik Fellwhisper worked to sabotage the talks.

events.text: The performer Braelin Wyngard was captured by a night hag while exploring a wandering isle.
cites: Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn, с. 188

events.text: Jarl Olfsvenn of Norland learned the location of the lost ring of Cymrych Hugh in the wreck of the Silverhand, and sought to acquire it for High King Derid Kendrick.

events.text: The Rusting appeared along the coast at Kythyss on the southern tip of Alaron.
cites: Forgotten Realms: Adventures in Faerûn, с. 187

events.text: Malefice Mortum was a ritual devised by Szass Tam at or just prior to the turn of the 16th century DR, which he plotted to use to conquer Thay.
In the year 27900 DR, the fire giants of this kingdom established twelve mighty fortresses along the shore of the Dragon Sea.
